Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms mean:

1. Region is the City of Palopo. 2. Mayor is the Mayor of Palopo. 3. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governance which is the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of the City of Palopo which is positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of the City of Palopo. 6. Regional Agency is a Regional Apparatus of the City of Palopo which includes the Regional Secretariat, the Secretariat of the Regional House of Representatives, Regional Offices and Regional Technical Institutions. 7. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including those still in the womb. 8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence which include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict and the State. 9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence. 10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family members, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, the community, the police, the prosecutor's office, the courts or other parties. 11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are economically and/or sexually exploited, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance (drugs) abuse, children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of physical and/or mental violence, children who are victims of conflict who experience physical violence and trauma, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of abuse and neglect. 12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically. 13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities for the recovery of victims. 14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect. 15. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or is likely to result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully. 17. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or bodily defects in a person, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. 18. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person. 19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 20. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or because of an agreement or contract is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person. Neglect also applies to anyone who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 21. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 22. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence. 23. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 24. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services by involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors. 25. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an institution for the recovery of victims of violence from health, education and economic independence aspects. 26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with established operational standards. 27.

Article 25

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, orders the promulgation of this Regional Regulation by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Palopo City. www.www

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL.

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy household life, society, nation and State. Therefore, the Palopo City Government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Human Trafficking, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection. Regional Government Administration prioritizes the implementation of Mandatory Government Affairs related to Basic Services as stipulated in Article 11 paragraph (3) juncto Article 18 of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. One of the Basic Services referred to is empowerment and protection for women and children from acts of violence.

On that basis, the Palopo City Government has taken steps to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence occurring in the social life of society, especially to women and children. The causes include, among others, the low level of public understanding of the rights of women and children, handling is not well coordinated, implementation is not sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to respond to and provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from all forms of acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from prevention of acts of violence to handling victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support from the government, Regional Government as well as community participation from the business sector and the community.

It is our hope that all forms of acts of violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Palopo City.

d. fostering and enhancing the economic independence of women victims of violence.
(3) Partnerships as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be stipulated in the form of an Agreement.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL.

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy household life, society, nation and State. Therefore, the Palopo City Government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Human Trafficking, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection. Regional Government Administration prioritizes the implementation of Mandatory Government Affairs related to Basic Services as stipulated in Article 11 paragraph (3) juncto Article 18 of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. One of the Basic Services referred to is empowerment and protection for women and children from acts of violence.

On that basis, the Palopo City Government has taken steps to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence occurring in the social life of society, especially to women and children. The causes include, among others, the low level of public understanding of the rights of women and children, handling is not well coordinated, implementation is not sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to respond to and provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from all forms of acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from prevention of acts of violence to handling victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support from the government, Regional Government as well as community participation from the business sector and the community.

It is our hope that all forms of acts of violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Palopo City.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL.

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy household life, society, nation and State. Therefore, the Palopo City Government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Human Trafficking, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection. Regional Government Administration prioritizes the implementation of Mandatory Government Affairs related to Basic Services as stipulated in Article 11 paragraph (3) juncto Article 18 of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. One of the Basic Services referred to is empowerment and protection for women and children from acts of violence.

On that basis, the Palopo City Government has taken steps to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence occurring in the social life of society, especially to women and children. The causes include, among others, the low level of public understanding of the rights of women and children, handling is not well coordinated, implementation is not sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to respond to and provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from all forms of acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from prevention of acts of violence to handling victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support from the government, Regional Government as well as community participation from the business sector and the community.

It is our hope that all forms of acts of violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Palopo City.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL.

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy household life, society, nation and State. Therefore, the Palopo City Government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Human Trafficking, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection. Regional Government Administration prioritizes the implementation of Mandatory Government Affairs related to Basic Services as stipulated in Article 11 paragraph (3) juncto Article 18 of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. One of the Basic Services referred to is empowerment and protection for women and children from acts of violence.

On that basis, the Palopo City Government has taken steps to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence occurring in the social life of society, especially to women and children. The causes include, among others, the low level of public understanding of the rights of women and children, handling is not well coordinated, implementation is not sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to respond to and provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from all forms of acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from prevention of acts of violence to handling victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support from the government, Regional Government as well as community participation from the business sector and the community.

It is our hope that all forms of acts of violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Palopo City.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL.

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy household life, society, nation and State. Therefore, the Palopo City Government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Human Trafficking, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection. Regional Government Administration prioritizes the implementation of Mandatory Government Affairs related to Basic Services as stipulated in Article 11 paragraph (3) juncto Article 18 of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. One of the Basic Services referred to is empowerment and protection for women and children from acts of violence.

On that basis, the Palopo City Government has taken steps to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence occurring in the social life of society, especially to women and children. The causes include, among others, the low level of public understanding of the rights of women and children, handling is not well coordinated, implementation is not sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to respond to and provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from all forms of acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from prevention of acts of violence to handling victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support from the government, Regional Government as well as community participation from the business sector and the community.

It is our hope that all forms of acts of violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Palopo City.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL.

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy household life, society, nation and State. Therefore, the Palopo City Government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Human Trafficking, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection. Regional Government Administration prioritizes the implementation of Mandatory Government Affairs related to Basic Services as stipulated in Article 11 paragraph (3) juncto Article 18 of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. One of the Basic Services referred to is empowerment and protection for women and children from acts of violence.

On that basis, the Palopo City Government has taken steps to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence occurring in the social life of society, especially to women and children. The causes include, among others, the low level of public understanding of the rights of women and children, handling is not well coordinated, implementation is not sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to respond to and provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from all forms of acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from prevention of acts of violence to handling victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support from the government, Regional Government as well as community participation from the business sector and the community.

It is our hope that all forms of acts of violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Palopo City.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms mean:

1. Region is the City of Palopo. 2. Mayor is the Mayor of Palopo. 3. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governance which is the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of the City of Palopo which is positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of the City of Palopo. 6. Regional Agency is a Regional Apparatus of the City of Palopo which includes the Regional Secretariat, the Secretariat of the Regional House of Representatives, Regional Offices and Regional Technical Institutions. 7. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including those still in the womb. 8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence which include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict and the State. 9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence. 10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family members, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, the community, the police, the prosecutor's office, the courts or other parties. 11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are economically and/or sexually exploited, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance (drugs) abuse, children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of physical and/or mental violence, children who are victims of conflict who experience physical violence and trauma, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of abuse and neglect. 12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically. 13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities for the recovery of victims. 14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect. 15. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or is likely to result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully. 17. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or bodily defects in a person, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. 18. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person. 19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 20. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or because of an agreement or contract is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person. Neglect also applies to anyone who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 21. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 22. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence. 23. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 24. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services by involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors. 25. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an institution for the recovery of victims of violence from health, education and economic independence aspects. 26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with established operational standards. 27.

The community may conduct monitoring of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence organized by the Regional Government through the mechanism of conveying aspirations to the Mayor or to the DPRD.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL.

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy household life, society, nation and State. Therefore, the Palopo City Government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Human Trafficking, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection. Regional Government Administration prioritizes the implementation of Mandatory Government Affairs related to Basic Services as stipulated in Article 11 paragraph (3) juncto Article 18 of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. One of the Basic Services referred to is empowerment and protection for women and children from acts of violence.

On that basis, the Palopo City Government has taken steps to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence occurring in the social life of society, especially to women and children. The causes include, among others, the low level of public understanding of the rights of women and children, handling is not well coordinated, implementation is not sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to respond to and provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from all forms of acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from prevention of acts of violence to handling victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support from the government, Regional Government as well as community participation from the business sector and the community.

It is our hope that all forms of acts of violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Palopo City.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 19

(1) The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector in the protection of women and children victims of violence.

(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out through:

a. notification of information on employment opportunities for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for women victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence whose education has been interrupted; and
d. fostering and enhancing the economic independence of women victims of violence.
(3) Partnerships as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be stipulated in the form of an Agreement.

CHAPTER VII

RIGHTS OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

Article 2

Letter a

The principle of humanity becomes the foundation of the concept of protection for women and children victims of acts of violence, constitutes respect for human rights as well as the dignity of every citizen and resident of Indonesia proportionally (the second principle of Pancasila).

Letter b

The principle of justice and gender equality, that gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, governmental activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.

Letter c

The principle of non-discrimination, that in providing protection to women and children victims of acts of violence there is no differentiation on the basis of age, gender, race, ethnicity, tribe, religion and between groups.

Letter d

The principle of best interests for victims, that all actions concerning women and children carried out by families, communities and Regional Government to fulfill the rights of women and victims of acts of violence as stipulated in laws and regulations.

Letter e

Article 3

The implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence is intended to provide protection and empowerment for women and children victims of violence.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms mean:

1. Region is the City of Palopo. 2. Mayor is the Mayor of Palopo. 3. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governance which is the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of the City of Palopo which is positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of the City of Palopo. 6. Regional Agency is a Regional Apparatus of the City of Palopo which includes the Regional Secretariat, the Secretariat of the Regional House of Representatives, Regional Offices and Regional Technical Institutions. 7. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including those still in the womb. 8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence which include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict and the State. 9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence. 10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family members, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, the community, the police, the prosecutor's office, the courts or other parties. 11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are economically and/or sexually exploited, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance (drugs) abuse, children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of physical and/or mental violence, children who are victims of conflict who experience physical violence and trauma, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of abuse and neglect. 12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically. 13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities for the recovery of victims. 14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect. 15. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or is likely to result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully. 17. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or bodily defects in a person, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. 18. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person. 19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 20. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or because of an agreement or contract is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person. Neglect also applies to anyone who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 21. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 22. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence. 23. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 24. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services by involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors. 25. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an institution for the recovery of victims of violence from health, education and economic independence aspects. 26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with established operational standards. 27.

(2) P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1), shall function as an integrated service center in providing protection to women and children victims of violence.

(3) Further provisions regarding the Organization and Working Procedures of

P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be regulated by

Mayor's Regulation.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL.

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy household life, society, nation and State. Therefore, the Palopo City Government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Human Trafficking, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection. Regional Government Administration prioritizes the implementation of Mandatory Government Affairs related to Basic Services as stipulated in Article 11 paragraph (3) juncto Article 18 of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. One of the Basic Services referred to is empowerment and protection for women and children from acts of violence.

On that basis, the Palopo City Government has taken steps to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence occurring in the social life of society, especially to women and children. The causes include, among others, the low level of public understanding of the rights of women and children, handling is not well coordinated, implementation is not sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to respond to and provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from all forms of acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from prevention of acts of violence to handling victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support from the government, Regional Government as well as community participation from the business sector and the community.

It is our hope that all forms of acts of violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Palopo City.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms mean:

1. Region is the City of Palopo. 2. Mayor is the Mayor of Palopo. 3. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governance which is the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of the City of Palopo which is positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of the City of Palopo. 6. Regional Agency is a Regional Apparatus of the City of Palopo which includes the Regional Secretariat, the Secretariat of the Regional House of Representatives, Regional Offices and Regional Technical Institutions. 7. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including those still in the womb. 8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence which include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict and the State. 9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence. 10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family members, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, the community, the police, the prosecutor's office, the courts or other parties. 11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are economically and/or sexually exploited, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance (drugs) abuse, children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of physical and/or mental violence, children who are victims of conflict who experience physical violence and trauma, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of abuse and neglect. 12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically. 13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities for the recovery of victims. 14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect. 15. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or is likely to result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully. 17. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or bodily defects in a person, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. 18. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person. 19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 20. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or because of an agreement or contract is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person. Neglect also applies to anyone who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 21. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 22. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence. 23. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 24. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services by involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors. 25. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an institution for the recovery of victims of violence from health, education and economic independence aspects. 26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with established operational standards. 27.

Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to respond to and provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from all forms of acts of violence that occur.

Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governance which is the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of the City of Palopo which is positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of the City of Palopo. 6. Regional Agency is a Regional Apparatus of the City of Palopo which includes the Regional Secretariat, the Secretariat of the Regional House of Representatives, Regional Offices and Regional Technical Institutions. 7. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including those still in the womb. 8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence which include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict and the State. 9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence. 10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family members, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, the community, the police, the prosecutor's office, the courts or other parties. 11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are economically and/or sexually exploited, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance (drugs) abuse, children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of physical and/or mental violence, children who are victims of conflict who experience physical violence and trauma, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of abuse and neglect. 12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically. 13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities for the recovery of victims. 14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect. 15. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or is likely to result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully. 17. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or bodily defects in a person, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. 18. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person. 19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 20. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or because of an agreement or contract is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person. Neglect also applies to anyone who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 21. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 22. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence. 23. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 24. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services by involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors. 25. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with established operational standards. 27.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL.

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy household life, society, nation and State. Therefore, the Palopo City Government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Human Trafficking, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection. Regional Government Administration prioritizes the implementation of Mandatory Government Affairs related to Basic Services as stipulated in Article 11 paragraph (3) juncto Article 18 of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. One of the Basic Services referred to is empowerment and protection for women and children from acts of violence.

On that basis, the Palopo City Government has taken steps to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence occurring in the social life of society, especially to women and children. The causes include, among others, the low level of public understanding of the rights of women and children, handling is not well coordinated, implementation is not sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to respond to and provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from all forms of acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from prevention of acts of violence to handling victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support from the government, Regional Government as well as community participation from the business sector and the community.

It is our hope that all forms of acts of violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Palopo City.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL.

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy household life, society, nation and State. Therefore, the Palopo City Government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Human Trafficking, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection. Regional Government Administration prioritizes the implementation of Mandatory Government Affairs related to Basic Services as stipulated in Article 11 paragraph (3) juncto Article 18 of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. One of the Basic Services referred to is empowerment and protection for women and children from acts of violence.

On that basis, the Palopo City Government has taken steps to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence occurring in the social life of society, especially to women and children. The causes include, among others, the low level of public understanding of the rights of women and children, handling is not well coordinated, implementation is not sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to respond to and provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from all forms of acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from prevention of acts of violence to handling victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support from the government, Regional Government as well as community participation from the business sector and the community.

It is our hope that all forms of acts of violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Palopo City.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL.

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy household life, society, nation and State. Therefore, the Palopo City Government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Human Trafficking, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection. Regional Government Administration prioritizes the implementation of Mandatory Government Affairs related to Basic Services as stipulated in Article 11 paragraph (3) juncto Article 18 of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. One of the Basic Services referred to is empowerment and protection for women and children from acts of violence.

On that basis, the Palopo City Government has taken steps to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence occurring in the social life of society, especially to women and children. The causes include, among others, the low level of public understanding of the rights of women and children, handling is not well coordinated, implementation is not sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to respond to and provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from all forms of acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from prevention of acts of violence to handling victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support from the government, Regional Government as well as community participation from the business sector and the community.

It is our hope that all forms of acts of violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Palopo City.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out through:

a. notification of information on employment opportunities for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for women victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence whose education has been interrupted; and
d. fostering and enhancing the economic independence of women victims of violence.
(3) Partnerships as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be stipulated in the form of an Agreement.

Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect. 15. CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL.

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy household life, society, nation and State. Therefore, the Palopo City Government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Human Trafficking, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection. Regional Government Administration prioritizes the implementation of Mandatory Government Affairs related to Basic Services as stipulated in Article 11 paragraph (3) juncto Article 18 of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. One of the Basic Services referred to is empowerment and protection for women and children from acts of violence.

On that basis, the Palopo City Government has taken steps to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence occurring in the social life of society, especially to women and children. The causes include, among others, the low level of public understanding of the rights of women and children, handling is not well coordinated, implementation is not sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to respond to and provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from all forms of acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from prevention of acts of violence to handling victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support from the government, Regional Government as well as community participation from the business sector and the community.

It is our hope that all forms of acts of violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Palopo City.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL.

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy household life, society, nation and State. Therefore, the Palopo City Government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Human Trafficking, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection. Regional Government Administration prioritizes the implementation of Mandatory Government Affairs related to Basic Services as stipulated in Article 11 paragraph (3) juncto Article 18 of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. One of the Basic Services referred to is empowerment and protection for women and children from acts of violence.

On that basis, the Palopo City Government has taken steps to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence occurring in the social life of society, especially to women and children. The causes include, among others, the low level of public understanding of the rights of women and children, handling is not well coordinated, implementation is not sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to respond to and provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from all forms of acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from prevention of acts of violence to handling victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support from the government, Regional Government as well as community participation from the business sector and the community.

It is our hope that all forms of acts of violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Palopo City.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms mean:

1. Region is the City of Palopo. 2. Mayor is the Mayor of Palopo. 3. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governance which is the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of the City of Palopo. 6. Regional Agency is a Regional Apparatus of the City of Palopo which includes the Regional Secretariat, the Secretariat of the Regional House of Representatives, Regional Offices and Regional Technical Institutions. 7. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including those still in the womb. 8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence which include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict and the State. 9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence. 10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family members, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, the community, the police, the prosecutor's office, the courts or other parties. 11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are economically and/or sexually exploited, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance (drugs) abuse, children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of physical and/or mental violence, children who are victims of conflict who experience physical violence and trauma, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of abuse and neglect. 12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically. 13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities for the recovery of victims. 14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect. 15. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or is likely to result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully. 17. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or bodily defects in a person, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. 18. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person. 19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 20. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or because of an agreement or contract is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person. Neglect also applies to anyone who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 21. CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL.

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy household life, society, nation and State. Therefore, the Palopo City Government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Human Trafficking, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection. Regional Government Administration prioritizes the implementation of Mandatory Government Affairs related to Basic Services as stipulated in Article 11 paragraph (3) juncto Article 18 of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. One of the Basic Services referred to is empowerment and protection for women and children from acts of violence.

On that basis, the Palopo City Government has taken steps to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence occurring in the social life of society, especially to women and children. The causes include, among others, the low level of public understanding of the rights of women and children, handling is not well coordinated, implementation is not sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to respond to and provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from all forms of acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from prevention of acts of violence to handling victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support from the government, Regional Government as well as community participation from the business sector and the community.

It is our hope that all forms of acts of violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Palopo City.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL.

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy household life, society, nation and State. Therefore, the Palopo City Government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Human Trafficking, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection. Regional Government Administration prioritizes the implementation of Mandatory Government Affairs related to Basic Services as stipulated in Article 11 paragraph (3) juncto Article 18 of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. One of the Basic Services referred to is empowerment and protection for women and children from acts of violence.

On that basis, the Palopo City Government has taken steps to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence occurring in the social life of society, especially to women and children. The causes include, among others, the low level of public understanding of the rights of women and children, handling is not well coordinated, implementation is not sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to respond to and provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from all forms of acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from prevention of acts of violence to handling victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support from the government, Regional Government as well as community participation from the business sector and the community.

It is our hope that all forms of acts of violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Palopo City.

Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically. 13. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 22. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence. 23. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 24. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services by involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors. 25. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an institution for the recovery of victims of violence from health, education and economic independence aspects. 26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with established operational standards. 27.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL.

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy household life, society, nation and State. Therefore, the Palopo City Government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Human Trafficking, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection. Regional Government Administration prioritizes the implementation of Mandatory Government Affairs related to Basic Services as stipulated in Article 11 paragraph (3) juncto Article 18 of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. One of the Basic Services referred to is empowerment and protection for women and children from acts of violence.

On that basis, the Palopo City Government has taken steps to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence occurring in the social life of society, especially to women and children. The causes include, among others, the low level of public understanding of the rights of women and children, handling is not well coordinated, implementation is not sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to respond to and provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from all forms of acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from prevention of acts of violence to handling victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support from the government, Regional Government as well as community participation from the business sector and the community.

It is our hope that all forms of acts of violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Palopo City.
